summary: Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Lama Zolpa Trinlé. He served as principal teacher at the shedra of Rumtek Monastery and spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery in 1992.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche studied under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He taught at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (1960–1970), founded Nyingmapa Wishfulfilling Center (1971), and taught at the University of Virginia (~1979–1980).

Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying under teachers including Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He held a teaching position at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and taught at Men-Tsee-Khang.
Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Khunu Rinpoche studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das, Sönam Gyaltsen, and Dev Narayan Tripathi. He served as a teacher at Men-Tsee-Khang.
Khyenrab Norbu was active in Tibetology. He studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen.

id: P:Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé
summary: Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé studied under Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Ki-yong Rhi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions at Dongguk University, where his affiliation is attested in 1983 and he was attested as professor emeritus in 2007.

Active in Buddhist studies, Kiattisak Ponampon completed an MA at the University of Otago supervised by Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie (attested 2015). In 2013, he also studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and others.

Kichinosuke Ito studied philosophy at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909) and the University of Freiburg (1920). He served at the University of Tokyo (1911–1918; professor 1923–1945), Hokkaido University (dean 1947, 1950–1951), and Chuo University (professor 1951–1958).
Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a PhD from Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Kim Knott held posts at the University of Leeds (~1984–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012).

Kim Plofker specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at Brown University (1995) under David Pingree and held appointments at MIT (2000–2004), Utrecht University (2004–2005), and Union College (2007, 2012, associate professor 2019).

Kimberley C. Patton works in religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Harvard University and held faculty posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1991) and Harvard University (~2001), also serving as an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (1991).

Kimiaki Tanaka specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo (-2008), where he was an assistant (~1984–1988), and later held posts at Keio University and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Kimmo Koskenniemi studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu and worked in computational linguistics. At the University of Helsinki, he served as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and directed the BAULT research community (attested 2015).
Kin Cheung works in Buddhist studies and religious studies, earning a PhD at Temple University under the supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).
King Chung Lo specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completing a PhD at the University of Leipzig under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco in 2009.
King Pong Chiu specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Manchester under the supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).

Kirby Flower Smith worked in Indology and other fields. He earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins University (1889), where he was a professor (~1889–1918), and served as Director of the American Academy in Rome (1914–1915).
Kirill Solonin works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts as professor at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) and Renmin University of China (~2013).
